source.title: Inferring Functionality of Attention Heads from their Parameters

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies a different, parameter-projection method to assess name-copying functionality in heads previously associated with IOI, including heads in GPT-2 small and GPT-2 medium. It does not reproduce the original circuit’s causal interventions or criteria.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own MAPS results on IOI-associated name-copying heads and the reported prompt-specific dynamic scores. The paper’s broader relation experiments and its causal ablations of other relations are not IOI circuit tests; results cited from the original IOI study are not recorded as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: A parameter-projection method (MAPS) checks whether heads named in the IOI circuit (GPT-2 small) and in the GPT-2 medium IOI circuit have the copying or suppression roles assigned to them. It bears on the head-role part of V1 and on V3, without causal circuit criteria.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say MAPS identified all previously reported IOI name-mover and negative name-mover heads (GPT-2 small) and Mover heads (GPT-2 medium). They found extra name-copying heads that 'may not participate' in the discovered circuits, and noted that one such head's dynamic score depends on the prompt context.
record.recipe_differences: Uses vocabulary-space projections of head parameters and dynamic output-score comparisons, rather than the original circuit’s head ablations, activation patching, or faithfulness, completeness and minimality tests.
record.method_sensitivity: For GPT-2 small head 8.11, the dynamic name-copying score is 0.23 with “This is a document about ⟨s⟩” and 0.92 with a name-copying demonstration prompt.

fits_no_version.finding: Extra heads outside the circuit (21 in GPT-2 small, 31 in GPT-2 medium) copy names by their parameters. Head 8.11's dynamic copying score varies with the prompt (0.23 vs 0.92).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Name-copying capacity is spread over many heads beyond the IOI circuit, and is expressed depending on context.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The IOI-specific evidence is primarily parameter-based classification, not a causal test of IOI performance or the complete circuit. The paper does not establish that additional name-copying heads participate in IOI, or that backup heads take over after ablation. It reports prompt-dependent dynamic scores for one additional head.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant IOI circuit result was omitted. General MAPS relation correlations, relation-head ablations on non-IOI tasks, and results cited from prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: Faithfulness, completeness and minimality; the duplicate-token, induction, previous-token and S-inhibition head classes; any causal role in IOI.
Other model families, sizes beyond GPT-2 medium, and checkpoints; causal reuse for other tasks.
Circuit-finding methods, ablation types and metrics are not compared.

missing.what: Each of the five GPT-2 small name-mover and negative name-mover heads also implements many other relations (parameter-level multifunctionality). In GPT-2 medium, Mover heads also implement year-to-following, country-to-capital, country-to-language and copying.
missing.locator: Section D, both subsections; Section 4.4 'Comparison with known head functionalities'

missing.what: Five heads labelled Mover in Merullo et al. Fig. 2 (14.5, 17.10, 16.0, 18.12, 21.7) were excluded from the authors' GPT-2 medium count. Their MAPS classification is not reported.
missing.locator: Section D, 'Mover heads in GPT-2 medium'

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is weak and non-causal: OV vocabulary projections only. Wang et al. themselves ran a similar OV analysis. R5's two missed backup heads are better read as a MAPS threshold limit than as a failure of the circuit, so no limits_scope label was given. The GPT-2 medium circuit comes from Merullo et al., not from this study.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the full 26-head, 7-class circuit, faithfulness, completeness or minimality, nor verify the head roles with the original circuit’s patching or ablation criteria.
Does not test whether backup heads take over after main name-mover ablation.

Tests name-copying classifications for GPT-2 medium heads, but not whether a complete IOI circuit carries the task there, across sizes or checkpoints. It does not causally establish reuse of components for other tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types or evaluation metrics.
Does not test whether the IOI circuit’s faithfulness or completeness depends on ablation, metric or prompt distribution.
Does not test the circuit across IOI name orders, templates or sentences with more names.
